name: The Simpsons Game
description: Create a PS5-ready The Simpsons Game folder from your Xbox 360 game files, with graphics settings and optional frame generation.
author: ZazaMastro
release_notes:
The first public release of The Simpsons Game PS5 Builder, by LoZazaMastro.

Choose your Xbox 360 ISO/XISO or extracted game files, configure the game, then create a complete PPSA74207 folder to transfer to your PS5.

Features
- A standalone Windows builder. An English WPF interface with a resizable dark window, yellow controls and a bundled .NET runtime.
- ISO and extracted-folder support. Accepts Xbox 360 regional editions through Title ID 45410809, without a Media ID whitelist.
- PS5 graphics options. Adjust rendering, shadows, FSR 1, FXAA, eyes, outlines, anisotropic filtering and colours. The default profile uses 4K, 3× rendering, 60 FPS gameplay, 30 FPS menus and English game language.
- Experimental frame generation. Supply your own Lossless.dll to enable 60/120 FPS targets or 2×, 3× and 4× generation with Auto target.
- In-game controls. Open the English quick menu with L1 + R1 + Options. Frame generation, colours and VSync can be changed during play; other settings are marked when they need a restart.
- Detailed logs. Open the log folder or export diagnostics from the builder.

L1 + R1 + L3 + R3 toggles frame generation for the current session. Release all four buttons before pressing again. Use the menu switch to save that choice for future launches.

Getting started
Download TheSimpsonsGame-PS5-Builder.exe from the assets below. Select your game source and a new output location, review the settings and build. Transfer PPSA74207 to /data/homebrew/PPSA74207 and mount it with ShadowMountPlus.

Your game files and Lossless.dll are not included. The EXE includes its .NET runtime and the PS5 executable and Home assets from version 3.10.5.

Native game and menu rates are limited to 30 or 60 FPS. Frame generation adds images without increasing the simulation rate and may cause input delay or visual artifacts. A compatible display and connection are needed for 120 Hz output. Menus use the selected render resolution; a separate native resolution for menus is not supported.
